1.sofaString: 108	Pt, ******, is a 2 1/2 year old female who is diagnosed with non-mosaic ****** syndrome and HLHS s/p ******* and ***** who is being referred for heart transplant Psychosocial Assessment.  Information for this assessment was obtained through an interview with the pt's parents and review of the medical records.   SW spent 60 minutes of face to face time with patient and family.     Living situation:  **, ******, lives with her parents and infant sister in ********, *******.  They reside in a single family home.  Their home has city water and central heating and a/c.  They replace the air filters monthly.  There is no smoking in the home.  They have 2 dogs, a ***** mix and a **** tzu mix.         Demographics:  Mother: ******* ****  DOB:  **/**/****           Age: 31  Employment:  Receptionist for Woman's Care ******* (no PTO, but does have FMLA)  Phone:  ***-***-**** (cell)     Father: ******* ******  DOB:  **/**/****   Age: 30  Employment:  Manager at *** ******* (has a small amount of PTO available)  Phone:  ***-***-****     Siblings:  Sister: ******** ******  Age 4 months     Support systems:  The parents are not married but have been engaged since ******** ****.  They disclose that they have a close supportive relationship and help each other get through the challenging times related to ******'s medical issues.  They also disclosed that both of their mothers reside nearby and are also supportive.  The maternal grandmother, **** *****, resides near *******'s work. She is currently keeping ******** while both parents are here with ****** for inpatient evaluation.  The paternal grandmother, ******* *********, resides in *******. She comes and keep ****** for a half day each week.       Both parents own a vehicle and state transportation to and from Gainesville will not be a problem.  However, they do state that travel expenses could become overwhelming, especially if they are missing work, due to the loss of income that will create.  ******* does not have PTO but is eligible for FMLA.  ******* has a small amount of PTO available.  Both parents hope to keep working as much as possible. They are hopeful that ****** will be able to remain at home while waiting for transplant.  Fundraising through **** was discussed, and the family verbalizes an interest in doing this.  An application for First Hand Foundation ***** will also be provided.         The family is supported entirely by the employment income of both parents.  ******* disclosed that they were not eligible for SSI for ****** because they are over-income.  ****** is covered by CMS ******** insurance.     ****** attends **** daily.  *** ******** **, OT, and ST there.  Although she has some delays, she is making progress.  She is able to verbalize multiple words.  She is also progressing with fine and gross motor skills, and appears to be meeting these developmental milestones as well.     Course of illness:     ****** is a 2 ½ yr old female with non-mosaic ****** syndrome and HLHS.  She has had ******* and ***** palliation surgeries.  She was doing well until about 4 weeks ago, when she was found to have a decrease in ventricular function as well as moderate tricuspid regurgitation.  Her local cardiologist then referred her for transplant evaluation.         Financial Situation:     ****** is covered by CMS.  The family is supported by the employment incomes of both parents.  They are typically able to meet their financial obligations.  However, they admit that increased expenses associated with transplant as well as decreased income will create financial stress. They are interested in fundraising.       Displacement housing was also discussed.  ******* verbalized desire to commute back and forth for follow up care if permitted.  She states that would decrease the disruption to the family, and allow dad to continue to work.  Mom is hopeful to be able to work some as well.  If they need to stay closer to ***********, ******* advised that they have family in ****** that they could stay with.       Family History:     The family denies any history of substance abuse or mental health issues.  The only involvement they have had legally is for traffic violations.  They deny any history with DCF.  They deny any other medical problems in the family.       Adherence:  There are no concerns for adherence that have been identified.  ******* and ******* have been providing care for ****** throughout her life.  They are comfortable administering meds and state that ****** does well taking them. ****** is able to take pills by mouth if she can chew them.  ****** previously had a g-tube and the parents were able to provide adequate care for that as well.  The family appears to be very involved in her care and have demonstrated good recall for her past medical history.  They appear to be good historians.  They have been compliant with keeping appointments and are attentive to changes in ******'s behavior that could indicate a change in her medical condition.  They have been good about seeking medical help when these changes have occurred.  They have also been observed to participate with the medical team in calming ****** during procedures (echo, getting temp taken, etc).          Assessment and recommendations:     Parents report that they were just advised of the possibility of transplant about 3 weeks ago.  They state this was initially a shock.  However, they state they have processed this and are both in agreement with moving forward with transplant if that will be the best thing for ******.  The family appears to have adequate support to assist in caring for ****** or for her infant sister.  The family does appear to have some unrealistic expectations regarding not missing much work at the time of transplant.  Further education will be helpful regarding the typical length of stay for transplant and typical care needs during the first few months post-discharge from transplant.         IMPRESSION:     (Low Risk - 1; Moderate Risk - 2; High Risk - 3; Severe Risk - 4)     Home Environment/Transportation -  1     Family Background & Social Support -  1     Financial/Insurance  - 2     Mental Health/Substance Abuse - 1     Involvement with *** Enforcement/Child Protection -  1     Adherence - 1     Understanding of medical situation & transplant process -  2     Health Literacy -  1     Coping Skills - 1     Total:  11 Low Risk     The family scores as low risk in regards to psychosocial contra-indicators to transplant.       The primary concern is the financial impact on the family if they are missing a lot of work.    Recommendations are listed below:     Recommendations:  *Provide ongoing education to the family about heart transplant and post-transplant care.  Use teach-back method to ensure that the family understands what is being explained.  *Provide fundraising and financial resources to assist the family with displacement expenses that arise secondary to transplant          ****** ******** LCSW  Pediatric Heart/ Lung Transplant Team  ***-***-****
